summary: BRAINSTORM/bsG_ternary_weinberger.md already writes the ES words as determinant/ideal data (form (x,1,y) of det d, ideals of Z[√−d] dividing 1+√−d) and shows that the quadratic field moves with the slice, so no single class group exists and no Weinberger/class-number sum. z31_quadratic_forms.md (c) records the same, and LITERATURE_2026 §(iii) adds that ES failure is not a subgroup condition on Cl(−4p) (193, 2521). The alt step (does the BC correspondence (x+z)(y+z)=N+z² keep track of xyz?) also fails: xyz is not a class invariant of the disc −4N form, and on ES N=4xyz/n moves with the solution.

The first step asked whether some ES slice is exactly a ternary representation problem. TWO_FIBRES (J)48, cited in z31_quadratic_forms.md §(c), already gives one: ES-five(p) ⟺ some path binary attached to X_p is NOT represented by I₃ = x²+y²+z², a one-class genus, so this is purely local; T1 is the statement that every odd-square path lattice embeds. The ineffective Duke–Schulze-Pillot route is blocked as recorded there (F2: the Eisenstein main term is a power for forms but ≍ log²p for ES; F3: there is no fixed form), and FRONTIER §6 lists local+spinor⇒global as true at odd squares.

THREE_SQUARES.md (O217, review R224) does the genus-theory comparison in depth: ES-five(p) ⟺ an admissible divisor with (A/p)=−1, where uncleanness is free at non-squares and the ES content is the admissibility gap; it also states the 3SQ conjecture. The item's ‘G1 matrix’ is the thick-object × extraction-rule generator matrix in BRAINSTORM/z52_deep_thin_pointwise_opus.md §2.0. Gauss three squares is the cell (class group of −4n, genus/exact-identity rule), and that cell is already T1-dead per FRONTIER §6 (local+spinor⇒global is true at odd squares). Bright–Loughran's no-local-obstruction is already used as the sanity check.

Verified via the arXiv API: Colliot-Thélène–Wittenberg (arXiv:0911.3539) prove there is no BM obstruction to integral points on x³+y³+z³=a (a≢±4 mod 9) or on x³+y³+2z³=a, and Booker (arXiv:1903.04284) found k=33 by search. The ES counterpart (Br U_n/Br Q ≅ Z/2, no BM obstruction for n≥2) is already Bright–Loughran, so the alt step that computes the Brauer group with the CTW setup is done (FRONTIER §1). Heuristic comparison: for three cubes the count up to height B grows like c_k log B with unbounded height, while ES at fixed n is a finite search with ≍ log²n expected solutions (M_BM). Neither world has a pointwise proof technique, so nothing transfers.

Graham's proof gets n>77 by splitting moves (1/x → 1/2x + 1/2x-type replacements, n ↦ 2n+c) that change the number of terms; with a fixed term count (3) there is no splitting move. Within (★) words 4uBC−u−B=n, the only scaling move (C ↦ aC) sends n ↦ an+(a−1)(u+B), which depends on the solution and is not an affine map of n. The alt step ‘test which affine maps preserve solvability for n≤10⁵’ is vacuous (ES holds there); a solution-level polynomial transfer n ↦ 2n+1 would prove ES by induction and is excluded by the Mordell–Schinzel/B1 picture.

Rewrote (★)/Type II in Znám form: (4uC−1)(4BC−1)=4Cp+1 says A | 4C·p+1, A′ | 4C·p+1, 4C | AA′−1, p | AA′−1. This is a mixed-sign Znám/Sylvester system on (A,A′,4C,p), and its Egyptian form 1/(4Cp) − 1/(AA′) = 1/(4Cp·AA′) is just the trivial identity 1/N − 1/(N+1) = 1/(N(N+1)). Sun Qi's k≥5 constructions are Sylvester-type recursions on the whole tuple; they have no free numerator and no gadget forcing a prescribed member p, so the Znám form adds nothing beyond the divisor form.

BRAINSTORM/s3_min_scale.md has the least-certificate census to 10⁷: h_min (least Type II modulus) has mean 8.8, max 2495, max h_min/log³p = 0.81. It is compared with g_box, the least prime ≡3 (4) with (p/g)=−1, essentially the least non-residue. A rerun (scripts/z52b_p1_H01_hmin_lnr.py 1e7) adds that for p≡1 (8), h_min ≥ lnr(p) always (the clean-level mechanism, THREE_SQUARES §1) and median h_min tracks the next primes ≡3 (4) above lnr (11, 23, 23, 23, 23, 47, 47 for lnr = 11…31). Within a fixed-lnr bucket the max grows with p (see Z0379), so the certificate is not controlled by the least non-residue alone.

Computed F_m(x), the fraction of n≤x with n≡1 (mod m) (the shape of 4Cp+1) and no divisor d≡−1 (mod m), d≤√n, for m=4C up to 100 and x up to 10⁹. It is not a Ford-type interval law: the slope dlogF/dloglogx is −0.50 exactly for m=4 (Landau: all prime factors ≡1 mod 4) and drifts toward −1/2 for larger m (m=8: −0.43, 24: −0.28, 100: −0.09 at 10⁹). So the fixed-m failure density is ≍(log x)^{−1/2}, set by the kernel of an odd real character mod m, i.e. the genus/BM ‘clean level’ layer already in THREE_SQUARES §1. ES needs one n over all m, which Ford's entropy count over n does not address.

BRAINSTORM/covering_distortion_dual.md (O150) already reads BBMST Thm 1.1/3.1 and Hough against the ES identity menus. Findings there: no finite covering, unconditionally (odd-square classes are never covered); the raw ES system violates the BBMST η<1 hypothesis, because Mordell classes give conditional removed mass 1 at 2, 3, 5, 7; the uncovered density is already quantified by OMEGA13 (log 1/δ*(T) ≍ 𝓛³ up to (log𝓛)^5); and the Hough-type minimum modulus statement is POINTWISE_TAIL Thm 2.1. The BBMST bound computed on the menus is exactly the comparison the item asks for, so nothing is new.

BRAINSTORM/apollonian_reciprocity.md (O144) read HKRS v3 and proved two things. Prop B.1: the BM set of the Type I locus and of the Type II locus is each non-empty at every prime. Prop B.2: there is no quartic or higher Brauer class over Q (BL Cor 2.7). The HKRS mechanism needs an infinite thin-group orbit, which ES at fixed n lacks. It also ran the alt numerical test (dividing-0068/translate-0093): the odd Type I/II zeros ≤2·10⁷ are the odd squares plus the coordinate artefact 105, with no u·m² (u≠1) or quartic family, and there is no quartic-character bias ((2/p)₄, (3/p)₄) in counts for 158k primes.

ZAREMBA_TRANSFER.md already treats the bounded-length/dual form. Its Thm A is known in substance from Chang's 'Partial quotients and equidistribution' Thm 5 and from Larcher: most primitive roots, which are non-residues and hence carry a character condition, give Σa_i ≪ log p loglog p. It concludes that the gap to λ≤3 is unchanged; FRONTIER §6 (J)95 records the thin-orbit route as reaching only λ ≍ log p log log p. The alt count #{a: λ(a/p)≤3 with ES₅ constraints} ~ c·log²p is the ES₅ BM main term with constant 45/(8π²) (BOARD2_SLATE Prop 3.4/Thm 3.5). Bourgain–Kontorovich (arXiv:1107.3776, verified) is density-one, i.e. B6.

BRAINSTORM/z31_markoff_chen.md (Chen arXiv:2011.12940 read) separates the two axes: Chen/BGS is a fixed surface with varying reduction prime, while ES is a family in n, the axis where Ghosh–Sarnak find Hasse failures. MARKOFF_ES.md §2 shows the two integral Vieta involutions on S_{n,D} both fix C, so integral points are fibrewise Pell orbits with no orbit-size invariant. apollonian_reciprocity.md notes that the fixed-n equation is linear in each variable. The alt searches for a non-permutation group action (free_opus-0029, tools-0121) are therefore answered: the only extra automorphisms are the fibrewise Vieta/Pell moves, and they preserve the C-level.

The item's premise (certificate at level d ⟺ Frobenius of p in a fixed S_d) is false as stated. At fixed (c,d,f) the certificate is a residue class of p mod 4cdf (Mordell); at fixed level it is a condition on the divisors of the p-dependent integer dp+1 or p²+4c²d, not a splitting condition of p in a fixed field. bsB_rayclass_norm_pullback.md proves that in the ray class field of Q(√−tp) only norm-pulled-back Dirichlet characters see the event, and y10_clean_level_classification.md gives the exact Cox-style statement (T1-type ⟺ tp+1 primitively represented by x²+ty²; clean ⟺ by a form of disc −4t). The density of p with a certificate at small level is the h_min table (s3_min_scale; rerun in Z0230/Z0379).

Wrote the sum: Σ_{a²+b⁴≤X} Λ(a²+b⁴) R(a²+b⁴) = Σ_{(u,C)} Σ_{a²+b⁴≡−u (mod 4uC−1)} Λ. This needs primes of the thin sequence a²+b⁴ in progressions to moduli up to ~√X (hyperbola symmetry), far beyond what Friedlander–Iwaniec (arXiv:math/9811185, verified: asymptotic for Λ on a²+b⁴) control. Even if it worked it would only give an average, i.e. almost-all ES on that thin set (B6). The known exceptional-set bound N·exp(−c(log N)^{3/4}) does not imply that, because it exceeds the size N^{3/4} of the sequence, but it is not a pointwise statement either.

Checked the abstracts via the arXiv API. HV I (1108.0096) gives the mean of R(n;a) over n with a fixed, and over both; HV II (1109.2274) gives the second moment and an Erdős–Kac law for log R(n;a) (mean log3·loglog n), i.e. R(n;a) behaves like d(n²). Jia (1109.0867) sharpens c₀(a) in S(N;a)=3/(π²a)∏(p−1)/(p+1)·N(log²N+c₁log N+c₀). At fixed p the ES count is Σ_x R(px; 4x−p), a sum along the sparse curve (a,n)=(4x−p,px) in which n and a are tied. Box mean values over n (fixed a) or over (a,n) say nothing about that curve, so no correlation estimate can be extracted.

The fixed-p lattice-point form is PARITY_AUDIT Lemma 2.1: R(p) = Σ_𝓡 1[(4uC−1)|p+u] with |𝓡| = (p/4)log p + O(p) and main term (log p)²/8 + O(log p). Its error needs a saving of p^{1−o(1)} at fixed p, a dead end listed in FRONTIER §6 (Weil/Selberg–Hooley/bilinear fixed-modulus savings), whereas exponent-pair hyperbola errors are power-size against a log² main term. The alt d ↔ (nx)²/d symmetry/parity is the known fact that R(p) is even (twice the count with d<√(4Cp+1), FRONTIER §2.1); its mod-2 refinements are INVOLUTION_ES.md (D).

BRAINSTORM/s8_twisted_hyperbola_thue.md (O258) is exactly the ‘bilinear Thue lemma’ step. ES-II ⟺ a point of the hyperbola Xε≡u (mod p) at height c with X ≡ −1 (mod 4cu); Thue/Minkowski need a lattice, and pigeonhole bounds the height but not the class, whose modulus is tied to the height (B2). Small solutions of xy≡a reach only p^{3/4} (Shparlinski). FRONTIER §6 lists ‘pigeonhole across shifts’ as dead (SS8 Lemma 2.3). The alt parity law for R(p) mod 2 is INVOLUTION_ES.md Lemma 2.1/(D), and the windmill form is WINDMILL (J)2 Thm 6.1.
